Description - RefreshFileUrl

Returns a new signed url for a file whose link expired. Works for own files without a prior agreement in the session; unknown ids give Ok with url nil. expire was nil in every reply (whether the server ever fills it: Unknown). The reply echoes id; realId came back as 0 for a playlist copy whether 0 or -1 was sent, so the realId sent is ignored when the id is valid.

**expire in the client:** parsed only from this reply, only when non-empty, and only in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss (local time; a Unix time, an ISO T, fractions or a zone suffix leave the previous value). It serves only the warning shown when the user pauses downloads ("%n file(s) are going to expire…", threshold [downloader] warn-before-expire in seconds: application default 3600, default config 60); as implemented the comparison computes now - expire, which looks inverted (Inferred bug). There is no proactive refresh: an expired link is detected when the HTTP download fails.

When the client sends it: when a download link has expired; session-bound.

Routing. The path item declares the server http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=, so this operation resolves to http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/RefreshFileUrl. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the SOAPAction header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (.svc/RefreshFileUrl) does not work (a:DestinationUnreachable, see soapRestStylePath).

Wire format. POST with Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8 (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers text/xml; charset=utf-8) and SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/RefreshFileUrl (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (Content-Encoding: gzip).

Path notes

SOAP operation RefreshFileUrl. The path-level server makes the URL routable: WCF dispatches on SOAPAction and ignores the ?op=/RefreshFileUrl query.

Schema RefreshFileUrlRequestEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required RefreshFileUrlRequestEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 request envelope for RefreshFileUrl: <s:Envelope><s:Body><RefreshFileUrl xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/">…. No SOAP header is ever sent; xmlns:i is declared on the operation element only when a nil value is present.

    • @s:encodingStyle string optional = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/" namespace http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

      SOAP 1.1 encodingStyle attribute. The real client always writes it; the service accepts the envelope with or without it.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one operation element; no other content (this also makes the per-operation envelopes mutually exclusive).

      • <RefreshFileUrl> object required RefreshFileUrlRequest xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

        Operation element RefreshFileUrl in http://chomikuj.pl/ (trailing slash is mandatory: with http://chomikuj.pl the parameters are not matched, see Service/wrong-operation-namespace).

        • <token> string required Token

          Session token. Always the first child.

        • <id> integer (int64) required

          File id.

        • <realId> integer (int64) required

          Real id (0 for own files in the captures; the client's "unused" value is -1). Ignored by the server when id is valid: 0 and -1 give the same reply.

        • <disposition> string required Disposition

          The client always sends download; player.audio also returns a url.

200

SOAP response envelope. HTTP 200 is used for every service-level outcome, including errors: check RefreshFileUrlResult/status. Compressed (Content-Encoding: gzip) when the request accepts gzip.

Schema text/xml

Schema RefreshFileUrlResponseEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required RefreshFileUrlResponseEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 response envelope for RefreshFileUrl: <s:Envelope><s:Body><RefreshFileUrlResponse xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/"><RefreshFileUrlResult …>.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one response element; no other content.

      • <RefreshFileUrlResponse> object required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/
        • <RefreshFileUrlResult> object required RefreshFileUrlResult

          Result element; declares xmlns:i (XML Schema instance, for i:nil) and xmlns:a.

          • <a:status> string required Status xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Outcome of the call. The client accepts only Ok; BadToken triggers a re-login, anything else is an error.

            7 values
            • "Ok" Success. The only value the client treats as success.
            • "BadToken" Unknown, logged-out or otherwise invalid token. The client re-authenticates (Auth) once per message (message-relog-count=1) and resends the message with the new token; session-bound messages are dropped.
            • "Forbidden" Auth: user name does not exist. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "PermissionError" Auth: wrong password for an existing user. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "Error" Generic failure. Usually carries a reason in errorMessage (e.g. EmptyName, NameExistsAtDestination); FolderFiles with an unknown disposition returns Error with errorMessage nil (FolderFiles/invalid-disposition).
            • "NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder" RemoveFolder with force=false on a folder that contains files, or on an unknown/removed folder id.
            • "WrongDisposition" FolderFiles: the disposition is a known value but not allowed for this call (download).
          • <a:errorMessage> string required nullable (i:nil) ErrorMessage xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Error detail for status=Error; nil otherwise.

          • <a:id> integer (int64) optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            File id; nil on BadToken.

          • <a:realId> integer (int64) optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Real id; 0 for a playlist copy whatever realId was sent.

          • <a:expire> string optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Link expiry: nil in every reply observed. The client accepts only yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss (local time) and uses it only for the pause warning.

          • <a:url> string optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Fresh signed download URL; nil for unknown ids.

500 SoapFault

WCF SOAP fault (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, not compressed). Possible for every SOAP operation: an empty or malformed body gives a:InternalServiceFault, an undeserialisable value a:DeserializationFailed, an unknown or missing SOAPAction a:ActionNotSupported. Operations with an operation-specific captured fault document it inline instead.

Schema text/xml

Schema SoapFaultEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required SoapFaultEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 fault envelope (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, never gzip-compressed).

    • <s:Body> object required
      • <s:Fault> object required SoapFault

        The fault.

        • <faultcode> string required no namespace

          Qualified fault code with its own namespace declaration on the element: a:InternalServiceFault and a:DeserializationFailed (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/net/2005/12/windowscommunicationfoundation/dispatcher), a:ActionNotSupported and a:DestinationUnreachable (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2005/05/addressing/none).

        • <faultstring> object required no namespace

          Human-readable message. DeserializationFailed names the parameter and CLR type, which is how the contract was established.

          • @xml:lang string required namespace http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace

            Language of the message (en-US).

          • text content string required

            Message text.

Captured live on 2026-10-24T15:25:07Z: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8.

A value that cannot be parsed as the parameter type (Int32) gives a:DeserializationFailed naming the parameter; the operation body never runs. This oracle was used to discover every parameter name/type/order.

Client vs live - discrepancies

Where the client's expected behaviour and the live service disagree, the spec follows the live behaviour (x-discrepancies):

  • 01: expire:str, format unknown; the client parses only yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss. Live it is always nil.

Security notes - findings that concern RefreshFileUrl

  • S-08 Low Signed File.aspx?e=…&pv=… download URLs are reusable bearer URLs (repeat GET and Range work); expire was always empty, so their lifetime is unknown.

From x-security-notes in the spec. Ratings and scope are explained on Security & privacy.
